title: Did We not open up your chest for you?
subtitle: A heart made wide enough to carry the mission
then: Sent just after Ad-Duha, when the people who once honoured the Prophet ﷺ had turned to mockery and abuse. Ibn Kathir says opening the chest means {reward}We illuminated it and made it spacious, vast and wide{/reward}. He cites: whomever Allah wills to guide, {idea}He opens his breast to Islam{/idea}.
now: Your chest feels tight: the deadline, the sick parent, the argument at home. You pray for the problems to vanish. {reward}Sometimes the answer is a heart made bigger, so the same weight fits.{/reward}
old: I will only feel at peace when my problems go away.
new: Allah can widen my heart so it holds what I am carrying.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to widen your chest for what you carry.

title: And We lifted your burden off you.
subtitle: The second blessing: a weight removed
then: Ibn Kathir explains the burden through the verse: {reward}that Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future{/reward}. The surah introduction speaks of {trap}a heavy weight on his back{/trap} from before his call.
now: You carry an old mistake around like a backpack you never take off. It is there at work, at dinner, in bed. {reward}Allah's forgiveness is described as lifting it off.{/reward} You are allowed to put it down.
old: I have to carry my past mistakes forever.
new: Allah removes burdens; I can ask Him to lift mine.
try: Name one old regret to Allah in a private dua and ask Him to take it off you.

title: It was a weight that pressed down on your back.
subtitle: Allah names how heavy it really was
then: More than one of the early scholars said this means {trap}its burden weighed heavy upon you{/trap}. {idea}Allah does not just lift the weight, He names how heavy it was.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was being told he had been seen.
now: You tell friends you are fine. Nobody sees the nights you lie awake. {idea}Allah's words here show He knows exactly how heavy it got.{/idea} You do not have to explain it to Him.
old: No one understands how heavy this is for me.
new: Allah knows exactly how much my burden weighs.
try: Tell Allah tonight, honestly, how heavy something feels. Do not soften it.

title: And We raised your name high.
subtitle: The third blessing: a mention that never stops
then: Mujahid said it means: {reward}I am not remembered except that you are remembered with Me{/reward}. Qatadah said no one gives a sermon, declares the Shahadah, or prays without saying his name. {trap}At that time he was being ridiculed in Makkah.{/trap}
now: You hear the adhan from a phone app in an airport lounge, or a mosque down your street. His name is in it. {reward}A man mocked in his own city is now named in every prayer.{/reward} Allah decides whose name rises.
old: If people look down on me now, that is how it will stay.
new: Allah raises names; the mockery of the moment is not the last word.
try: Next time you hear the adhan, listen for his name and send salawat on him ﷺ.

title: Said twice: with hardship comes ease.
subtitle: The repeat that turns a promise into certainty
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}informs that with difficulty there is ease, then reaffirms it by repeating it{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ was in the hard early years. {reward}The repeat leaves no room for doubt.{/reward}
now: You read the first line and think: nice words. Then it comes again, straight after. {reward}Allah is saying it twice because He knows you need to hear it twice.{/reward} The ease is already packed in with this hardship.
old: Ease might come one day, if I am lucky.
new: Allah said it twice: the ease is coming with this hardship, not instead of it.
try: Write both lines on a note and put it where you will see it during your hardest hour.

title: When you are done with work, stand up for Allah.
subtitle: What to do with the time you get free
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}when you have completed your worldly affairs and broken from their routine, get up to worship{/idea}, with zeal and a pure intention. Mujahid said: {reward}when you are free, stand up for your Lord{/reward}.
now: The laptop shuts at six. The next three hours usually vanish into a sofa and a screen. {idea}This verse asks for a slice of that freed-up time.{/idea} Even ten minutes on the prayer mat counts.
old: After work, my time is just for switching off.
new: The time I get free is a chance to stand before my Lord with a clear head.
try: Tonight, once your tasks are done, pray two rakahs before you turn on any screen.

title: And to your Lord, turn all your longing.
subtitle: Where hopes should finally point
then: Ibn Kathir joins this to the verse before: stand for worship and {idea}purify your intention and desire for your Lord{/idea}. After the blessings and the promise of ease, {reward}the surah ends by pointing every hope to Allah{/reward}.
now: You hope for the promotion, the reply to your message, the test result. Those hopes are not wrong. {idea}The verse asks you to send them to the right address.{/idea}
old: My hopes rest on what people decide for me.
new: Every hope I have is best sent to my Lord.
try: Take the thing you are most hoping for this week and ask Allah for it by name.
